stories.headline: One killed, one injured in shooting on Denver's Federal Boulevard following verbal altercation
stories.summary:
Denver police are investigating a double shooting in the 1700 block of Federal Boulevard that left one man dead and a woman hospitalized early Monday morning. Officers responded to the scene at 1:22 a.m. after authorities reported the incident, finding the man pronounced dead at the scene.

The woman was transported to a hospital and is expected to survive her injuries. Police said the shooting appears to have originated from a verbal argument that escalated.

No suspect has been identified or arrested. Investigators are asking anyone with information to contact Crime Stoppers at 720-913-7867.

stories.headline: Three people dead after suspected shooting and crash in Denver on Friday night
stories.summary:
A suspected shooting followed by a vehicle crash resulted in three fatalities in Denver on Friday night, according to CBS Colorado. The incident represents one of the city's deadlier single-event crime scenes in recent weeks.

Details on the identities of the victims and a suspect description had not been fully released as of the report's publication. Denver police were investigating the circumstances connecting the shooting and the subsequent crash.

The case adds to ongoing concerns about gun violence in Denver, where city officials have been tracking shooting incidents closely through the summer months.

stories.headline: State Rep. Manny Rutinel resigns from Colorado legislature to focus on competitive 8th Congressional District race
stories.summary:
Democratic state Rep. Manny Rutinel of Commerce City has resigned from the Colorado legislature to devote his full attention to his congressional campaign against Republican incumbent Rep. Gabe Evans in Colorado's 8th Congressional District. The 8th District, which covers communities north of Denver, is considered one of the most competitive House races in the state this cycle.

Rutinel secured the Democratic nomination for the seat and is now campaigning full time against Evans. The district has been closely watched nationally as a potential bellwether in the broader fight for control of the U.S. House.

Resigning from a legislative seat to run for higher office is not uncommon, but the move signals the intensity of the campaign and the resources Rutinel is committing to the race ahead of the November election.

stories.headline: Democrat Eileen Laubacher mounts long-shot bid to unseat Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th Congressional District
stories.summary:
Retired Navy Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher is running as a Democrat in Colorado's 4th Congressional District, attempting to flip what is widely considered the state's safest Republican seat currently held by Rep. Lauren Boebert. Laubacher, a former Republican turned unaffiliated voter, said she felt compelled to run to advocate for rural Coloradans who feel ignored by elected officials.

The district covers 38,000 square miles, including the Eastern Plains and Front Range counties such as Douglas, Larimer, Weld and Adams. Registered Republicans outnumber Democrats by more than two to one, though nearly half of voters are unaffiliated. Laubacher said she has traveled 28,000 miles through the district since launching her campaign last spring.

Laubacher brings a national security background to the race, having served 34 years in the Navy Reserve and U.S. Navy, deployed to Afghanistan, served as defense attaché at the U.S. Embassy in India, and worked as a senior director at the National Security Council under the Biden administration. The last Democrat to win the district did so in 2008.

stories.headline: GOP gubernatorial candidate Victor Marx campaigns on Western Slope as November race against AG Phil Weiser approaches
stories.summary:
Republican gubernatorial nominee Victor Marx is actively courting voters on the Western Slope as Colorado's November general election nears. Marx narrowly won a three-way primary, defeating two sitting state lawmakers after raising nearly $2 million more than his opponents combined from more than 20,000 donors.

Marx now faces Democratic nominee and current Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser in the general election. The Western Slope swing is part of a broader effort to consolidate Republican support in a region that has historically leaned conservative.

The governor's race is among the most consequential statewide contests on Colorado's November ballot, with Weiser holding the advantages of statewide name recognition and incumbency in state government.

stories.headline: Colorado clean energy sector reports $6.3 billion economic impact, driving job growth on Eastern Plains
stories.summary:
A new report by the Colorado Solar and Storage Association found that renewable energy has generated a $6.3 billion statewide economic impact and has become a major driver of employment in the state's Eastern Plains counties. Clean energy jobs in those 21 eastern counties grew from 4,316 in 2010 to 6,715 in 2024, making utility-scale energy the second-highest-paying job category in the region.

The industry projects an additional 3,594 jobs statewide over the next decade, with 961 of those in Eastern Plains counties, and an additional $1.7 billion in economic impact. Colorado law targets 80% renewable power generation by 2030, and state utilities are reported to be on track to meet that goal.

The findings come amid a tension between the state's renewable energy trajectory and federal policy under the Trump administration, which has encouraged a return to fossil fuels including extending the life of coal plants such as Tri-State Generation's Craig unit. The report emphasizes that counties such as Weld, which have also benefited from fossil fuel fracking, are simultaneously seeing gains from clean energy construction and maintenance employment.

stories.headline: Metro Denver home sales fall nearly 20% in August as mortgage rates and economic uncertainty weigh on buyers
stories.summary:
Home sales in the Denver metro area dropped nearly 20% in August compared to the prior year, as elevated mortgage rates and broader economic uncertainty continued to suppress buyer demand. The decline marks a significant cooling in what had been one of the nation's most active housing markets during the pandemic era.

Affordability remains a central challenge, with home prices still well above pre-pandemic levels even as sales volume has fallen. Analysts point to a combination of high borrowing costs and consumer hesitation tied to economic conditions as the primary factors limiting transactions.

The slowdown has implications for related industries including real estate services, home construction and mortgage lending across the metro region. Market observers will be watching whether any rate relief in coming months translates into renewed buyer activity before year's end.

stories.headline: New Broomfield housing complex opens for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, but demand vastly outpaces supply
stories.summary:
The Grove at Cottonwood, a new 40-unit affordable housing complex in Broomfield with services tailored for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, held its grand opening celebration on Sept. 2. Ten of the units are reserved specifically for people with IDD through the federal Section 811 program, while the remaining units are designated affordable housing that IDD residents can also apply for.

The development offers relief for families who have spent years seeking supported housing, but advocates say it barely scratches the surface of Colorado's need. Approximately 127,000 people with intellectual or developmental disabilities requested housing services from state agencies in 2022, and at least 20,000 people with IDD statewide live with aging caregivers without adequate supportive housing options available.

"We are not ready for the tsunami of people that are about to flood the system," said Desiree Kameka-Galloway, lead consultant of Neuro-Inclusive Housing Solutions. The complex was leasing out remaining units as of August, with full occupancy expected by mid-September.

stories.headline: Beulah community faces chronic flooding from Aspen Acres Fire burn scar the size of Denver
stories.summary:
The small southeastern Colorado community of Beulah is experiencing repeated, deadly flooding in the aftermath of the Aspen Acres Fire, which left behind a burn scar approximately the size of Denver. Burn-scarred ground repels water rather than absorbing it, causing runoff to funnel rapidly into communities below.

The flooding has complicated Beulah's water situation, affecting both water quality and infrastructure reliability in a community that was already strained by the fire itself. Burn scar flooding is a well-documented secondary disaster in Colorado, where large wildfires have become increasingly common amid drought and high temperatures.

Residents and local officials are working to address both the immediate flooding threat and the longer-term challenges of water supply and community recovery in the burn scar zone.

stories.headline: Mount Blue Sky's scenic byway wraps up first full visitor season since major renovation
stories.summary:
Mount Blue Sky's scenic byway — recognized as the highest paved road in North America — is completing its first full visitor season following a significant renovation that had previously curtailed public access. The byway draws large numbers of visitors to the Denver metro's high country each summer.

The renovation addressed aging infrastructure on one of Colorado's most iconic mountain drives, which reaches elevations above 14,000 feet. The successful completion of a full season is seen as a milestone for the site's return to full public access.

Mount Blue Sky, formerly known as Mount Evans, remains one of the most accessible fourteeners in Colorado and a popular destination for Front Range residents seeking alpine scenery.

stories.headline: Broncos gear up for Monday Night Week 1 opener in Kansas City after longest preseason-to-opener gap in team history
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos are preparing for their season opener against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football on Sept. 14, coming off an unusually long 17-day gap between their final preseason game and the regular season debut — the longest such stretch in franchise history. Head coach Sean Payton adjusted the team's practice schedule to account for the extended layoff, adding sessions on Monday and Wednesday while building in an extra rest day on Friday.

Denver returns all five offensive line starters, which the coaching staff regards as a key communication advantage for a road game at notoriously loud Arrowhead Stadium. The Broncos are 3-0 on Monday Night Football and 10-2 in extended-week games under Payton.

Linebacker Alex Singleton noted that five consecutive years of the same divisional matchup means both teams have deep familiarity with each other's tendencies. Bo Nix is at quarterback as the team defends its 2025 AFC West title, with the Broncos entering the season with high expectations following ownership stability under Carrie Walton Penner and Greg Penner.

stories.headline: CU Buffs and CSU Rams both open 2026 season 1-0; debate begins over which win was more impressive
stories.summary:
For the first time since 1996, both the Colorado Buffaloes and Colorado State Rams opened a football season with victories, with CU winning 14-13 over Georgia Tech in Atlanta and CSU defeating Wyoming to claim the Bronze Boot at home. The simultaneous 1-0 starts generated immediate comparisons between the two programs heading into Week 2.

Denver Post columnists Troy Renck and Sean Keeler debated the question, with Renck favoring CU's road win over a Power 4 opponent as more significant from a résumé standpoint. Keeler noted that the Massey Ratings — once part of the BCS formula — showed CU making the single largest jump of any FBS team nationally from Week 0 to Week 1, moving from No. 73 to No. 38, while CSU posted the fifth-largest jump in the country.

CU quarterback Julian Lewis was credited with a composed performance in the fourth quarter to secure the narrow victory. Both programs will host non-conference opponents in Week 2, with CU facing Weber State and CSU hosting Southern Utah, giving each team a chance to move to 2-0 for the first time since 1994.

topStory.headline: Houthi Strikes Ignite Saudi Oil Facilities, Wound 73 in Major Regional Escalation
topStory.summary:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched a wave of attacks early Tuesday against cities and energy infrastructure in southern Saudi Arabia, wounding at least 73 people and setting fire to multiple oil facilities and utilities. The strikes hit civilian and economic targets across four cities — Abha, Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait — temporarily halting operations at affected installations, according to the Saudi Energy Ministry. Saudi coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki confirmed the wounded included women and children.

Al-Malki, who also holds the rank of colonel in coalition statements, pledged that the Saudi-led coalition would 'take all necessary operational measures to deter this terrorist militia.' The Houthis, who control Yemen's most populous northern regions, have been launching attacks toward Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July and have also targeted Saudi vessels in the Red Sea. Tuesday's strikes followed warnings from Iranian officials that energy assets across the Gulf, including U.S. oil and gas interests, remained vulnerable.

The attacks sent oil prices to six-week highs, compounding existing pressure on global energy markets stemming from disruptions to shipping through both the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz. Before the current conflict, roughly one-fifth of all global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments transited the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has separately announced plans to establish a new restricted maritime zone in the Gulf, with Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warning that vessels entering the zone would face Iranian sanctions.

The escalation marks a significant widening of a conflict that has moved through repeated pauses and renewals since the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28, targeting Tehran's nuclear program and its support for regional proxy forces. The Houthi offensive also threatens to further strain the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a critical chokepoint for global oil and trade that has partially offset disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz. Commodity vessel movements slowed again this week as the cumulative effect of regional instability continued to weigh on shipping and supply expectations.
